question: A certain number of people are sitting in a row, facing the north. R sits third to the left of P. Q sits fourth to the right of P. Only two persons sit between Q and T. If no other person is sitting in the row, what is the total number of persons seated?
solution:
**Given:** A certain number of people are sitting in a row, facing the north

1) R sits third to the left of P.

2) Q sits fourth to the right of P. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aec51d93e482753effe0f5292077f4b2c46cdaba4d1bd26350eda4cd2c6b6648.png] 

3) Only two persons sit between Q and T.

As position of T with respect to Q is not known yet, therefore there are two possible cases.

Case 1)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d394f99717505e5408e80870574e46d47eab3497207276b0cbe28e471de65907.png] 

Case 2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/443591e2c0ef1fb69987c12e42c575ef03095cc41f444892546c798044a6c511.png] 

Thus, according to the final arrangement if no other person is sitting in the row, then the total number of persons seated in a row can be either 11 or 8.

As out of all the options only 11 is given, therefore case 2 will be eliminated.

Case 1)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d394f99717505e5408e80870574e46d47eab3497207276b0cbe28e471de65907.png] 

So the total number of persons seated in a row is 11.

Hence, **"Option 3"** is the correct answer.
